Clone vs Fork vs Branch
All three involve “copies” in some way.

Concept

Download repo locally

Safe parallel work

Open science is just science done the way science should be done….

In the future there will be science and closed science

The infrastructure school (better infrastructure ->better science)

When we publish scientific papers - we are expected to share (archive) R-code (or other code we are using to produce the reported results).

Never manually edit raw data
Raw data

Original source files
Untouched
Read-only if possible

Processed data

Cleaned data
Derived variables
Analysis-ready datasets

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
section: Scripts Are Better Than Manual Steps
text:
Scripts Are Better Than Manual Steps
Manual workflows are fragile
Problems with manual editing:

Difficult to track changes
Easy to introduce errors
Impossible to reproduce precisely
Hard to scale

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Scripts are documentation
Good scripts explain:

What was done
Why it was done
In what order

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Documentation Matters
Good projects explain themselves
Minimum documentation:
A README.md should explain:

What the project is
Where the data came from
How to run the analysis
Folder structure
Required software/packages

Future-you will appreciate this.

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Relative Paths
Avoid absolute paths!
Bad
read.csv("C:/Users/matt/Desktop/project/data.csv")
Better
read.csv("data_raw/data.csv")
Even better
here::here("data_raw", "data.csv")

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:

Absolute paths break collaboration
Absolute paths:

Only work on your computer
Break when folders move
Cause problems across operating systems

Relative paths:

Improve portability
Improve collaboration
Improve reproducibility

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Step 1 — Create a project
In RStudio:

File → New Project
New Directory
New Project
Name it:

wildlife_reproducibility_project

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Step 2 — Create folders
Create these folders:
/data_raw
/data_processed
/scripts
/outputs
/docs
Or create them using R:
folders <- c(
  "data_raw",
  "data_processed",
  "scripts",
  "outputs",
  "docs"
)

sapply(folders, dir.create)

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Step 3 — Add raw data
Download the workshop dataset from GitHub.
Save it into:
/data_raw

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Step 4 — Create a cleaning script
Create:
scripts/01_clean_data.R
Example:
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
wildlife <- read_csv(
  here::here("data_raw", "wildlife_data.csv")
)

wildlife_clean <- wildlife %>%
  filter(!is.na(count))
write_csv(
  wildlife_clean,
  here::here("data_processed", "wildlife_clean.csv")
)

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:
Step 5 — Create a figure
Create:
scripts/02_make_plot.R
Example:
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)

wildlife_clean <- read_csv(
  here::here("data_processed", "wildlife_clean.csv")
)

p <- ggplot(wildlife_clean,
            aes(x = habitat,
                y = count)) +
  geom_boxplot()

ggsave(
  filename = here::here("outputs", "habitat_plot.png"),
  plot = p,
  width = 6,
  height = 4
)

title: What Is a Reproducible Project?
text:

Create:
README.md
Include:

Project title
Short description
Folder structure
How to run the analysis
Required packages

Keep it simple

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
section: Open science is not reckless openness
text:
Open science is not reckless openness
Important question:

What should be open?

Not everything can or should be shared publicly.

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Ecological data can be sensitive
Examples:

Nesting sites
Endangered species locations
Poaching risks
Disturbance-sensitive species
Indigenous/community knowledge
Personal information

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Questions Before Sharing
Before sharing ask:

Could sharing create ecological harm?
Are there legal restrictions?
Does consent apply?
Could data be misused?
Are sensitive locations included?

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:

Analysis scripts
Simulated datasets
Metadata
Aggregated outputs
Quarto reports
Protocols
Workflow documentation

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Metadata Matters
Metadata = data about data
Metadata explains:

Where data came from
Sampling methods
Variable definitions
Units
Coordinate systems
Missing values

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Metadata Example
Variable: count
Description: Number of observed individuals
Unit: individuals
Missing values: NA = no observation recorded

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
FAIR Principles
(meta)Data should be:

Findable
Accessible
Interoperable
Reusable

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
What Is a Licence?
Licences explain reuse permissions
Without a licence:

reuse becomes unclear
collaborators may hesitate
legal uncertainty increases

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Sensitive Species Example
Example: endangered species locations
Publishing exact coordinates may:

Increase poaching risk
Increase disturbance
Damage vulnerable habitats

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Openness can be flexible
Possible approaches:

Share code only
Share aggregated data
Blur coordinates
Delay data release
Use controlled access

title: Sharing Data and Code Responsibly
text:
Good Sharing Checklist

Is the workflow reproducible?
Is metadata included?
Is sensitive information removed?
Is there a licence?
Would another person understand this?
